source.title: The Tangled Web They Weave: Exploring Neural Representations with Directed Simplicial Complexes

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study develops and evaluates directed simplicial complexes for small synthetic MLPs, but does not test whether neurons generally respond to unrelated inputs or test any of the listed claim versions. It discusses polysemanticity as motivation and reports a limited result about whether simplex membership identifies known polysemantic neurons.
record.gate_note: The reported sizes and dimensions of trained and untrained network complexes, circuit-method comparisons, and hyperparameter sensitivities measure properties of the proposed DSC construction, not the prevalence or causes of polysemantic neurons. They are not rows for the claim. The study does report a direct comparison of simplex participation for neurons in its handcrafted polysemantic network; that result is recorded under fits_no_version because none of the versions covers this particular proxy’s failure to identify known polysemantic neurons.
record.test_reason: The study builds directed simplicial complexes for tiny synthetic ReLU MLPs (one handcrafted to be polysemantic by construction) and evaluates the method. It never measures how often or why neurons respond to unrelated inputs in vision or language models. It also never tests causes, architecture effects or measurement dependence of polysemanticity. Polysemanticity is motivation only. The one polysemanticity-adjacent result concerns whether the DSC proxy identifies designed mixed neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors also stress that whether a neuron is monosemantic depends on the chosen elementary features, since a 45° rotation swaps the readings. They also state that larger networks and natural data are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces coherent counterfactual ablations and directed simplicial complexes; it does not reproduce the original neuron-visualization or SoLU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The constructed complexes vary with input distribution and some test settings. For handcrafted networks, varying selection tolerance changed simplex sets at range endpoints and changed filtration values; multiple-testing choices affected some trained-network complexes. These are sensitivities of the DSC construction, not measurements of polysemantic-neuron prevalence.

fits_no_version.finding: In the handcrafted [2,3,4,4] network, n7 is in 14 maximal simplices across four one-hot complexes, while the six coordinate-mixing neurons are in 2–7 each. Simplex participation therefore does not identify the designed polysemantic neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maximal directed-simplex participation is not a reliable indicator of designed polysemantic neurons in small MLPs.

record.problems: The experiments are confined to small ReLU MLPs on a synthetic task. The authors state that semantics are known only for the handcrafted networks and that further architectures and tasks are needed to determine whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons. The relevance test does not compare joint ablation effects with effects of individual predictors, and its multiple-testing error rate is not controlled jointly across dimensions, input sets, and networks.
record.rows_left_out: Complex sizes and dimensions, trained-versus-untrained comparisons, input-set distances, circuit-discovery comparisons, and hyperparameter sweeps are omitted because they characterize the DSC method or its outputs rather than measuring any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No image classifiers or visual inputs.
No transformer language models or token/context responses.
The bottleneck network is handcrafted to mix coordinates. Superposition as the cause is never tested on learned networks.
Random-init networks are compared only on DSC size, not polysemantic-neuron share.
No activation function, architecture or regularization comparison of polysemantic share.
Not studied. Footnote 5 only notes that semantic assignment depends on the chosen input basis.
The paper notes that rotating the input basis by 45° swaps the mono/poly reading. This is an argument, not a tested scoring or activation-range dependence.

record.verdict_notes: The basis-dependence remark (footnote 5, App. C.1) touches V7 conceptually but is a definitional observation, not a measured result. Trained-network neuron mixing (two of four first-layer neurons mix coordinates) is described qualitatively, without a polysemanticity measure.

versions.untested_parts: Image classifiers, InceptionV1, and responses to unrelated visual inputs are not studied.
Transformer language models, MLP neurons in language models, and token or context responses are not studied.
The study uses a handcrafted bottleneck network with mixed-coordinate units, but does not test whether superposition causes polysemanticity by packing more sparse features than available neurons.
The comparison with random initializations concerns DSC size and dimension, not whether initialization, regularization, or noise causes polysemantic neurons when capacity is sufficient.
No comparison of activation functions, modern architectures, SoLU, regularization effects on polysemantic-neuron share, or performance cost of reducing that share is made.
The study does not investigate whether unrelated input mixtures share a coherent feature or whether canonical polysemantic neurons have been misread.
The study varies input sets and DSC hyperparameters, but does not test how neuron polysemanticity classifications depend on activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: handcrafted [2, 3, 4, 4] polysemantic network
rows.operation_detail: Counted each neuron's participation in maximal simplices across the four one-hot input-set complexes.

conditions.value: four one-hot quadrant sets; aggregate across the four complexes

rows.measure: Maximal simplices containing each neuron, used to assess whether simplex participation identifies polysemantic neurons.
rows.value: n7 belongs to 14 maximal simplices across the four complexes; each of the six neurons described as mixing both coordinates belongs to between 2 and 7.
rows.note: The authors state that n7 represents Q4 and that simplex participation does not identify the polysemantic neurons in this example. This is a result about the proposed proxy, not a test of the listed claim versions.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The subject is a network handcrafted to be polysemantic, so this row measures the DSC proxy's ability to flag known mixed neurons. It does not show polysemanticity arising. The value is accurate: n7 is in 14 maximal simplices and the six mixed neurons in two to seven each (App. G.1).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
